new_statements.quote: Die Betonung wird mit Akut /´/, unbetonte Endungen in Tabellen ggf. mit Gravis /`/ [...] gekennzeichnet. Da im Zaz. Feminina auf -ε ~ -ɨ und -i im Auslaut unbetont sind, werden sie meistens als solche nicht angegeben, stattdessen wird die vorletzte Silbe betont gekennzeichnet, z.B. kέrgε „Henne“, kárdi „Messer“. [...] Bei Maskulina auf betontem -ε ~ ɨ, i oder u erübrigt sich ebenfalls die Angabe des Genus. (p. 19) — Ebenfalls taucht beim Akzentwechsel von der letzen auf die erste Silbe im Vokativ eine Labialisierung auf: Qεrεmán „Kahraman (Männername ‚Held')“ Rct. Sg. : Qέrεmu! Vok. Sg. (p. 61)
new_statements.translation: Stress is marked with an acute, unstressed endings in tables where necessary with a grave [...]. Since in Zazaki feminines ending in -ε ~ -ɨ and -i are unstressed word-finally, they are mostly not marked as such; instead the penultimate syllable is marked as stressed, e.g. kέrgε 'hen', kárdi 'knife'. [...] With masculines in stressed -ε ~ ɨ, i or u the indication of gender is likewise unnecessary. (p. 19) — Likewise, with the accent shift from the last to the first syllable in the vocative, a labialisation appears: Qεrεmán 'Kahraman (man's name, Hero)' rectus sg. : Qέrεmu! vocative sg. (p. 61)
new_statements.citation: Keskin, Mesut. 2008. Zur dialektalen Gliederung des Zazaki. Magisterarbeit, Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main. 204 pp. (open: https://www.zazaki.de/files/)
new_statements.locator: §4 Transkription, p. 19 (PDF p. 19); vocative remark p. 61 (PDF p. 61); syncope remark p. 114 (PDF p. 114)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (symlink to../diml1238/, 204 pp., text layer) and extracted PDF pp. 12, 19, 20, 61, 114 with extracted text. The quoted passages are there: p. 19 (§4 Transkription) reads verbatim "Die Betonung wird mit Akut /´/, unbetonte Endungen in Tabellen ggf. mit Gravis /`/,... gekennzeichnet. Da im Zaz. Feminina auf -ε ~ -ɨ und -i im Auslaut unbetont sind, werden sie meistens als solche nicht angegeben, stattdessen wird die vorletzte Silbe betont gekennzeichnet, z.B. kέrgε „Henne", kárdi „Messer"." Minor differences: the bridged sentence "Bei Maskulina auf betontem -ε ~ ɨ, i oder u erübrigt sich ebenfalls die Angabe des Genus." is at the top of p. 20, not p. 19; the vocative example on p. 61 i…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is on the final syllable by default (masculine stems ending in -e/-ɨ/-i/-u carry final stress and the author marks stress only where it deviates); the feminine endings -e/-ɨ/-i are inherently unstressed, so such feminines are stressed on the penult (kέrge, kárdi). The vocative moves the accent from the last to the first syllable; syncope of a weak ɨ shifts the accent one syllable leftwards (xálε vs Pülümür xalɨ́ε).
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed feminine endings -e/-ɨ/-i (penult stress); vocative with initial stress; accent retraction after syncope of weak ɨ; unstressed enclitics/postpositions (-dɨ, -i 'also') and unstressed inflectional endings noted in passing.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation/lexical forms in a dialectological transcription convention; the author states (p. 12) that prosody is deliberately not treated because of the state of research, so the final-stress default is implied by the marking convention rather than stated as a phonological rule. The remarks apply to Zazaki generally with Northern Zazaki (Dersim/Varto/Pülümür/Ovacık/Hozat) examples.
new_statements.identity_note: Keskin 2008 describes all Zazaki dialects with its main focus on Northern Zazaki (Dersim, Erzincan, Varto, Hınıs, Pülümür, Ovacık, Hozat) = kirm1248; the transcription statement is phrased for Zazaki in general, the vocative example is from the Northern (Dersim/Erzincan) area. The other full grammars are on the Southern dialect: Todd 1985 (Çermik/Siverek) and Paul 1998 Part I (Çermik-Siverek) = Dimli/Southern Zazaki, Glottolog diml1238; Paul 1998's 'Alevi-Dialekte' section is the Northern part. Selcan 1998 is Dersim (kirm1248) throughout.

sources.locator: §4 Transkription, p. 19 (PDF p. 19); vocative remark p. 61 (PDF p. 61); syncope remark p. 114 (PDF p. 114)
sources.note: Prosody explicitly excluded from systematic treatment (p. 12: 'auf die prosodischen Merkmale... gar nicht eingegangen'). Transcription note p. 19: stress marked with acute; feminines in final -e/-ɨ/-i are unstressed so the penult is marked (kέrgε 'hen', kárdi 'knife'), masculines have stressed final -e/-ɨ/-i/-u. p. 61: vocative shifts the accent from the last to the first syllable (Qεrεmán : Qέrεmu!). p. 114: accent shifts to the preceding syllable under syncope of weak ɨ (xálε vs Pülümür xalɨ́ε).

sources.note: Historical phonology/morphology only: the Old Iranian feminine -ā survives as unstressed -e [-ə] while some masculines have stressed final -e [-ˈKɛ] (§4.1, PDF p. 14); the infinitive suffix -ene [ˈɛnə] is initially stressed (§4.3, PDF p. 15). No general word-stress rule.
